t: The Hope Theatre was one of the playhouses built in and around London for English Renaissance drama, in the same company as the Globe, the Curtain and the Swan. Nothing of it is described as standing here now, so you're picturing it rather than seeing it. Its designer is named as Philip Henslowe, an Elizabethan theatrical entrepreneur and impresario. He matters today largely because his diary survives, and it's a key primary source on the theatrical world of Renaissance London.
